question: Under what circumstance does one behold a true vīra practitioner among courtesans?
premises: The practitioner is situated in the midst of courtesans.
The speaker poses a question of when such a hero is seen.
The object of vision is a sādhaka.
inference: A true vīra sādhaka is recognized when seen situated in the midst of courtesans.
uncertainties: The rhetorical force of kadā may imply rarity or a specific condition.
plain_english: When do I see a hero-practitioner who is situated in the midst of courtesans?
